title: Residual (non-regression) false positive: extractCommandSubstitutionSpans splic…
description:
Residual (non-regression) false positive: extractCommandSubstitutionSpans splices a preserved $(...) span back verbatim without recursively stripping quotes inside it, so inert quoted data nested in a double-quoted command substitution is still scanned. Verified: echo "$(grep -c 'x -eq 42' f)" flags on the branch. main flags it too, so this is not a regression and is out of the PRD's stated scope, but it is the same false-positive class US-001 exists to close. Consider either recursing (stripQuotedSpans on the preserved span) or extending the accepted-blind-spot bullet in patterns.md to name this shape alongside the -e case.
